plate_comment: Boot-time arming of the intake air heater performance test (called once from cm848_applicationMain): reloads the dwell from intake_air_heater_performance_test_baseline_sample_delay_ticks, zeroes the sample count, ring index and the baseline and loaded battery-voltage averages, and sets intake_air_heater_performance_test_state to 0 (armed) only when no battery temperature sensor fault (P0517 / P0516, fault_detected_bits_368_to_383 masks 0x800 / 0x1000) is set and the battery temperature and the intake manifold temperature differ by at most intake_air_heater_performance_test_arming_temperature_difference_limit (640 = 10 F, a cold-soaked engine); otherwise it sets state 6 (aborted). (was hpcr_throttlePositionDiagnostic)
evidence: Not a throttle diagnostic: it writes only the heater-test counters and intake_air_heater_performance_test_state (0 or 6), its one caller is the boot list of cm848_applicationMain, and cm848_monitorIntakeAirHeaterPerformance can only start from state 0. Masks 0x800 / 0x1000 of word 23 are P0517 / P0516 (battery temperature sensor) in the fault decode.

plate_comment: Called by states 1, 2 and 3 of cm848_monitorIntakeAirHeaterPerformance: returns 1 and sets intake_air_heater_performance_test_state to 6 (aborted) when the intake manifold temperature is below intake_air_heater_performance_test_minimum_intake_manifold_temperature (0 F), an intake air temperature sensor fault (P0113 / P0112) or a grid heater circuit fault (P0541 / P0542 / P2607 / P2608) is set, the battery voltage (1/16 V per count) is outside the range intake_air_heater_performance_test_minimum_battery_voltage to intake_air_heater_performance_test_maximum_battery_voltage (160 to 208 = 10 to 13 V), or intake_air_heater_status_flags shows neither preheat on (bit 1) nor preheat done (bit 3); otherwise returns 0. It does not measure a battery load. (was engine_protection_batteryLoad_check)
evidence: Verified from the code: every branch either aborts the test or returns 0, and the fault masks decode as intake-temperature (bits_16_to_31 0x8 / 0x10 = P0113 / P0112) and grid-heater (bits_288_to_303 0x40 / 0x80 / 0x100 / 0x200 = P0541 / P0542 / P2607 / P2608) circuit faults. ROM thresholds read from cm848_rom.bin: 0, 208, 160.

plate_comment: Phase group A call slot of the wastegate duty controller (called from cm848_phase_group_a_processing): calls cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest and does nothing else. (was cm848_turboCompensationWrapper)
evidence: The body is the single call cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest(), which writes rpm_governor_state_t_0040a3ca.commanded_rpm (21792 = 2 x 10896 in the dump reaches wastegate_solenoid_duty_command through cm848_applyWastegateSolenoidDuty). No CM550 function carries the turbo-compensation names, so no cross-firmware link breaks. The wave-1 G3 agent suggested cm848_runWastegateDutyControl; either spelling is fine.

plate_comment: Boot init of the wastegate duty controller (called from cm848_applicationMain): zeroes wastegate_duty_integrator_q16, governor_rpm_band_rate_working, the duty request of the controller state struct and the battery-voltage averaging accumulator ema_filter_state_t_003fa19c (coefficient pointer set to WORD_003ffcb4), and sets the twelve lookup hint words DAT_003fa17e to DAT_003fa19a to 2. (was mpc555_initTurboCompensationVariables)
evidence: Every variable it zeroes is used by cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest (integrator, rate-limiter state, commanded_rpm, the EMA state fed with sensor_readings_t.battery_voltage) and the 12 words set to 2 are exactly the interpolation hint arguments of that function. The wave-1 G3 agent suggested cm848_initWastegateDutyControl.

plate_comment: Anti-windup of the wastegate duty controller integrator: sets wastegate_duty_integrator_enable_flag (integrator enabled) to 0 while the duty request is pinned at the duty ceiling with a non-negative integrator input (wastegate_duty_integrator_input), or pinned at the duty floor with a non-positive input; otherwise to 1. Called once per pass by cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest. (was cm848_checkSpeedBandCondition)
evidence: Truth table of the nested tests: flag = 0 iff (commanded_rpm >= desired_rpm and input >= 0) or (commanded_rpm <= lower_rpm_limit and input <= 0); the flag gates the integrator update in cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest (conditional-integration anti-windup). Its only other user is that function.

Second reader of commanded_rpm: applies the override governor_commanded_rpm_override_cal (flag bit 0 of governor_rpm_override_flags), caps it at speed_control_rpm_upper_limit_cal (12800) and, with governor_status_flags mask 0x4000 (set in the dump), clamps it into [fuel_control_setpoint_cal, 12800 - fuel_control_setpoint_cal] = [1856, 10944]; fuel_control_setpoint_working = 10896 in the dump = commanded_rpm. The consumers (cm848_calculateSpeedControlRampUp / RampDown, cm848_updateSpeedControlOutputs, cm848_selectSpeedControlGains, cm848_checkSpeedZeroCondition) work in the same 12800 = 100 percent scale, but cm848_applyWastegateSolenoidDuty reads commanded_rpm directly and not their output, so whether this speed-control chain is wastegate duty conditioning or a separate governor path needs its own pass (the wave-1 G3 agent reached the same conclusion); no rename.

plate_comment: Charging regulator error: when engine_feature_enable_flags_cal bit 0 is set, saves the previous error in charging_voltage_error_previous, sets charging_voltage_error = charging_voltage_target - battery voltage (1/16 V per count; 48 = 3.0 V in the dump), updates charging_voltage_error_slow_average (new-sample weight charging_voltage_error_slow_average_coefficient / 65536) and sets charging_voltage_error_fast_component = error - slow average. (was cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset)
evidence: Direct reading of the code; the outputs are the inputs of the state 2 / 3 duty tables, the state machine and the PID. Dump: target 240, error 48. The wave-1 G3 agent suggested the same name.

plate_comment: Steps the 4-state charging (alternator field) regulator when engine_feature_enable_flags_cal bit 0 is set: saves the state in alternator_field_regulator_previous_state, then takes the next state from the 4-entry handler table at ROM 0x57730 (0 idle or fault, 1 start ramp, 2 regulation, 3 load response; the handlers at ROM 0x38338 / 0x38384 / 0x383f0 / 0x3844c are not decompiled as functions). (was cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode)
evidence: The body is exactly one indirect call through the handler table into alternator_field_regulator_state; I disassembled the four handlers (see the transition note). The wave-1 G3 agent suggested the same name.

plate_comment: Charging-voltage PID loop, run only when operating_mode_flags_cal mask 0x20 is set and the regulator is in state 2 or 3, where it replaces the duty of cm848_calculateAlternatorFieldDutyByRegulatorState: gain, integral rate and derivative rate come from the a set while charging_voltage_error is below alternator_field_duty_pid_gain_set_error_threshold and from the b set otherwise; the p term (error x gain), the integral term (integrator preset from the duty on the 1 -> 2 transition, clamped 0..25600) and the d term ((error - previous error) x rate) are summed, clamped to 0..25600 and written to alternator_field_duty_target. (was cm848_calculateProtectionOutputDemand)
evidence: Direct reading; all working variables (cruise_speed_roc_integrator, battery_voltage_p_term / d_term ...) are used only here and in the init, and the result feeds cm848_applyAlternatorFieldDuty. Dump calibration: threshold 4, gains 35 / 80, integral rates 65 / 5, derivative rates 0 / 0. The wave-1 G3 agent suggested cm848_calculateAlternatorFieldDutyPid; the ByPid spelling pairs with cm848_calculateAlternatorFieldDutyByRegulatorState.

plate_comment: Charging system voltage monitor: sets fault_detected_bits_368_to_383 mask 2 (P2504, voltage high) when the regulator is not in state 0, no protection voltage is active and charging_voltage_error_slow_average stays below charging_system_voltage_high_error_threshold (-16 = measured voltage more than 1 V above the target) for charging_system_voltage_high_confirm_passes passes (150) and a timer then counts charging_system_voltage_high_fault_count_limit passes (6); sets mask 4 (P2503, voltage low) after charging_system_voltage_low_confirm_passes passes (80) in regulator state 2 with the grid heater control in state 5 (shutdown) and battery voltage below charging_system_voltage_low_threshold (184 = 11.5 V); clears mask 4 after charging_system_voltage_low_clear_passes passes (50) above charging_system_voltage_low_clear_threshold (192 = 12.0 V). (was cm848_checkProtectionOutputConditions)
evidence: Not in the lead list; found while tracing the chain. Bits 1 / 2 of word 23 are P2504 / P2503 in the fault decode (high / low), matching the direction of each test; thresholds read from the RAM dump. Skip this row if the chain is reviewed elsewhere.

plate_comment: Alternator output test: in regulator state 2 with the grid heater in state 5 (shutdown), engine speed above battery_voltage_sample_rpm_threshold_cal, no charging fault set and charging_voltage_error_slow_average above battery_voltage_sample_threshold_cal it counts passes; once the count reaches battery_voltage_sample_count_max_cal a second counter starts and, when it equals battery_fault_sample_count_threshold_cal, the battery voltage is snapshotted and battery_voltage_fault_flag is set, which makes cm848_applyAlternatorFieldDuty cut the field duty to 0. The test clears if the voltage then falls by more than battery_fault_clear_delta_cal; otherwise after cruise_enable_count_threshold_cal passes it counts a failed test and releases the field, and fault 368 (P2502) is set when the failed tests reach cruise_confirm_threshold_cal. The thresholds in the RAM dump (8000 rpm, 640, 65535) keep it from ever tripping. (was cm848_processProtectionMode2)
evidence: Not in the lead list; behaviour read from the code. battery_voltage_fault_flag (0x40b264) is read in cm848_applyAlternatorFieldDuty, where it forces alternator_field_duty_target to 0 (xref_addr.py: 1 read there, 4 writes plus 1 read in this function, 1 write in the init), so the function really cuts the field and watches the voltage fall; thresholds read from the RAM dump. Skip this row if the chain is reviewed elsewhere.

Read only in regulator state 0 of cm848_calculateAlternatorFieldDutyByRegulatorState, where alternator_field_duty_target = this value, then forced to 0 unless fault_detected_bits_368_to_383 mask 1 (fault 368, P2502) is set; all four state handlers return to state 0 whenever that fault is set, and masks 2 / 4 (faults 369 / 370) do not select this value. 0 in the dump; 0x4087fa is outside the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal. The only direct setter of fault 368 found by a name grep is cm848_testAlternatorOutputByCuttingField, so the name says the fault number instead of a meaning.

0x3fd5ee is inside the EEPROM mirror 0x3fd482-0x3feec1 (EEPROM 0x16c holds the same word, 0x7ca6, as the RAM dump), so the name needs _cal. The PI integrator of cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest: error x gain / 100 added in 16.16 fixed point while the enable flag is set, clamped to the upper / lower limit words << 16, preset to -(rate-limited term) << 16 by the reset flag; zeroed in the controller init; dword in both users.
integrator >> 16 in cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest, the integrator contribution (half-duty counts) added to the base and rate-limited terms before the floor / ceiling clamp; no other user.

selected control term x integral gain >> 10, clamped to +-32767, written in cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest and the amount added to the integrator; its sign is the direction tested by the anti-windup in cm848_checkSpeedBandCondition. Used in those two functions only.

wastegate_integrator_gain_by_error_* lookup x throttle_rate_scale_factor_cal >> 12 in cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest, then multiplied into the control term for the integrator input; no other user.

Upper clamp of the wastegate duty integrator (value << 16 against the Q16 integrator); 10240 = 80 percent in half-duty counts in the dump; read only in cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest. 0x3ffc9c is above the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.

Lower clamp of the wastegate duty integrator; -12800 (word 52736) = -100 percent in half-duty counts in the dump; read only in cm848_calculateWastegateDutyRequest. Above the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.

Written from sensor_channel3_value, or sensor_channel3_default_value when the sensor channel 3 gate trips; the gate tests fault_detected_bits_16_to_31 masks 0x200 / 0x400 = P0108 / P0107 (the barometric pressure circuit faults in the fault decode) and a second fault gate on fault_detected_bits_336_to_351 mask 0x10. Lead from the wave-1 G3 agent, candidate name theirs.

State 2 handler (ROM 0x383f0) enters state 3 (load response) when charging_voltage_error_fast_component exceeds this; 192 (12 V) in the dump, i.e. state 3 cannot be entered in this calibration. Signed: lha read in disasm_func.py.

State 1 and state 3 handlers go to / stay in regulation (state 2) when charging_voltage_error <= this and stay in state 3 while the error is above it; 1 (1/16 V) in the dump. Signed: two lha reads in disasm_func.py.

cm848_monitorWastegateBoostPressure counts the high-boost fault only while wastegate_solenoid_duty_command <= this; 11520 = 45 percent of 25600 in the dump. e2m CWG_Driver_Duty_Cycle_Threshold (0x011B2E00, Duty cycle threshold for wastegate error check); the e2m CWG block at 0x011B2E00 lines up by relative offset with 0x409fe0 (+2 high boost time = wastegate_monitor_debounce_count_limit, +4 high load, +6 minimum engine speed = wastegate_monitor_minimum_engine_speed_threshold, +8 minimum start battery temperature). xref_addr.py says word (1 read / 0 writes), lhz.

The pass-window check of cm848_monitorWastegateBoostPressure requires engine_load_percent >= this; 19200 = 75 percent in 1/256 percent units in the dump. e2m CWG_High_Load_Threshold (0x011B2E04, %LOAD, 0.00390625, Percent load threshold for wastegate pass check). xref_addr.py says word (1 read / 0 writes), lhz.

cm848_initAdaptiveControl sets the monitor armed flag to (this <= battery_temperature_sensor_filtered); 1280 = 20 F (1/64 F) in the dump. e2m CWG_Min_Start_Battery_Temp_Threshold (0x011B2E08, DEG_F 0.015625, Min battery temp at start-up to run electronic wastegate rationality). xref_addr.py says word (1 read / 0 writes), signed lha in the code, so i16.

Byte set once in cm848_initAdaptiveControl (battery temperature at start >= the minimum start temperature) and read at the top of cm848_monitorWastegateBoostPressure, which returns while it is 0; 1 in the dump. xref_addr.py says byte (1 read / 1 write). Loaded into the dwell counter at the end of state 1 and gates the ring sampling of state 2; 30 in ROM (cm848_rom.bin). xref_addr.py: word (1 read / 0 writes).

Charging regulator transitions, from the disassembly of the handlers (ROM 0x38338 / 0x38384 / 0x383f0 / 0x3844c, lead confirmed): 0 -> 1 when engine speed >= word 0x4087a8 (3200 = 400 rpm) or cold_start_phase = 3, and fault 368 clear; every state returns to 0 when speed < word 0x4087a2 (2880 = 360 rpm) or fault 368 is set; 1 -> 2 when the duty is 25600 or charging_voltage_error <= word 0x4087ae (1); 2 -> 3 when charging_voltage_error_fast_component > word 0x4087ac (192, never in this calibration); 3 -> 2 when the duty is 25600 and alternator_field_load_response_elapsed_passes > word 0x4087b0 (11) or when the error is <= word 0x4087ae. The handlers are LAB_ code with no function definition, so they cannot be renamed.

Charging chain facts: the only direct setter of fault 368 (P2502) found by a name grep of fault_detected_bits_368_to_383 is cm848_testAlternatorOutputByCuttingField (an indexed write would not show), whose thresholds in the dump (8000 rpm at 0x4087ba, 65535 passes at 0x4087b6 / 0x4087b8 / 0x4087be, 640 at 0x4087c2) keep it from ever tripping, so alternator_field_duty_while_charging_system_fault_368_set is moot here. charging_voltage_error_slow_average_coefficient is 64881 / 65536 = 0.99, so the slow average follows the error almost one to one and the fast component stays near 0 (state 3 is effectively off). Still-misnamed a / b gain sets read only by cm848_calculateAlternatorFieldDutyByPid (no _cal outside the EEPROM mirror): battery_voltage_gain_a_cal / _b_cal (0x4087e8 / 0x4087ea = 35 / 80) = proportional gains for error below / at or above the threshold, battery_voltage_integral_rate_a_cal / _b_cal (0x4087de / 0x4087e2, dword = 65 / 5) = integral rates, battery_voltage_ema_rate_a_cal / _b_cal (0x4087d6 / 0x4087d8 = 0 / 0) = derivative rates; the other cruise_* / battery_voltage_* words in 0x4087b6-0x4087c2 belong to cm848_testAlternatorOutputByCuttingField; the RAM counters cruise_check_sample_count, cruise_monitor_timer, cruise_enable_sample_count(_b) and cruise_sensor_sample_count are charging monitor counters too. protection_fuel_output_target_prev (0x40b27e) is written (PID and init) and never read.
